The Wildhammer clan is a rugged, nature-dwelling branch of the dwarven race famed for taming wild gryphons and wielding storm-charged hammers. Driven from their ancestral fortress of Grim Batol centuries ago, they carved a fiercely independent home across the wooded peaks of the Hinterlands. Though reclusive by nature, they remain stalwart friends of the Alliance, defending the skies whenever called upon.

Before the War of the Three Hammers, the Wildhammers lived in the foothills around Ironforge. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died, civil war fractured the dwarven kingdom, and the victorious Bronzebeards claimed Ironforge for themselves. Thane Khardros led his clan north to establish a magnificent hold inside the peak of Grim Batol. Yet peace was short-lived: the defeated Dark Irons soon laid siege to the fortress. While Khardros personally slew the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud, her dying curse blighted the mountain so deeply that the halls became uninhabitable. Refusing an invitation to move back under Bronzebeard rule, the Wildhammers chose self-reliance, marching north into the forests and rocky crags of the Hinterlands.

In the lush highlands of their new realm, the Wildhammers built Aerie Peak. Unlike their subterranean cousins, these dwarves embraced the open sky and living rock, developing a deep, spiritual kinship with the native gryphons. Forging enchanted stormhammers in secluded aviaries, the Wildhammers became the finest aerial cavalry in Azeroth. During the Second War, when Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer pushed his forces toward Quel'Thalas and assaulted Aerie Peak, Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and the Alliance came to their aid. In gratitude, High Thane Kurdran Wildhammer pledged his gryphon riders to the coalition, dogfighting the Horde's enslaved red dragons across the skies of Lordaeron and the Great Sea.

When the Dark Portal reopened, Kurdran Wildhammer led his riders into Draenor with the Alliance Expedition, sacrificing his return to seal the rift—an act commemorated by a colossal statue in Stormwind's Valley of Heroes. Back in Aerie Peak, High Thane Falstad stepped up to lead the clan. Even as the human kingdoms squabbled and fractured in later years, the Wildhammers remained steadfast partners of King Terenas Menethil II. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron in the Third War, Wildhammer flyers took to the air once more, fighting desperately to protect allied lands and innocent refugees from the walking dead.

Worgen are fierce, lupine humanoids cursed with uncontrollable primal rage, moving upright yet hunting with bestial swiftness. Once thought to be mere nightmares conjured from other planes, these savage pack-hunters now terrorize Silverpine Forest, Ashenvale, and Duskwood.

Long before their recent emergence in Lordaeron and Kalimdor, wolf-men were whispered of in folktales and cautionary fables. Their true origins remain a mystery: scholars who have studied the beasts believe they were drawn into Azeroth from another realm, and both Archmage Arugal and the night elves' Scythe of Elune have proven able to call them forth.

During the Third War, as the Scourge hordes overran Lordaeron and slain Kirin Tor wizards rose again as undead, Archmage Arugal sought a weapon to bolster Dalaran's dwindling ranks. Drawing from the forbidden research of the Dalaran wizard Ur, Arugal pierced the veil and summoned the beasts into Silverpine Forest. The summoned worgen devastated the undead invaders with savage abandon, but the archmage could not leash their fury. The beasts turned on the wizards themselves, spreading their curse through fang and claw. Driven mad by guilt and fascination, Arugal adopted the monsters as his children, seizing Baron Silverlaine's ancestral seat—now rechristened Shadowfang Keep—and cursing nearby villagers into monstrous nocturnal servitude.

Across the sea in Kalimdor, another summoning unleashed the worgen anew. Desperate to purge the lingering demonic remnants of the Burning Legion from Felwood, the night elf Sentinel Velinde Starsong unearthed the Scythe of Elune. Channelling the ancient relic, she called forth wolf-men to tear apart the demonic satyrs.
